newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese trucks paralysed by Spanish strike.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese trucks paralysed by Spanish strike.

text.p: A strike by Spanish truck drivers has immobilised hundreds of Portuguese trucks and the businesses of many road transport firms could be put at risk if the stoppage goes on much longer, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

"We estimate that hundreds of Portuguese trucks are stranded in various parts of Spain and on the French-Spanish border," Carlos Cazenave, head of the National Association for the Transport of Goods by Road (ANTRAM), told Reuters.

By Wednesday, a week-long strike by Spanish truck drivers had spread to almost all of northern Spain, unions said. Strikers are mainly pushing for retirement at 60 years, instead of the current 65, and renegotiation of petrol costs.
With hundreds of Spanish trucks blocking main roads, foreign drivers found themselves caught up in the jam.
Cazenave said Spanish strikers had thrown rocks at passing Portuguese trucks.

The local news agency Lusa quoted the Portuguese consulate in San Sebastian in northern Spain as saying that a Portuguese trucker, Carlos Antunes Simoes, had been seriously injured in the head by a stone thrown at his vehicle.
Local television showed images of a 12-year-old Portuguese girl, a passenger in her father's truck, who was hit in the face by a stone, allegedly thrown by a Spanish striker.
"Stones have been thrown at Portuguese truckers and their tyres have been stabbed," Cazenave said. "We are convinced that the Spanish strikers are responsible."
Cazenave said dozens of Portuguese trucks were blocked in Santander and Bilbao in northern Spain.
He said Portuguese truckers stranded at Irun on the border between France and Spain were demanding guarantees for their safety before continuing their journeys.
"If this strike goes on for much longer, many businesses could be jeopardised," he said.
"Portugal suffers every time there is a strike elsewhere in Europe because of the impact on imports and exports," he added.
Portugal's truck fleet, which totals about 5,000 vehicles, imports and exports all kinds of produce ranging from machinery parts to shoes, textiles to electronics equipment and food.

Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Wednesday the Portuguese government would do all it could to help truckers who may seek help from Portuguese consulates in Spain, and expressed his solidarity with the victims of the strike.
"The Portuguese truck drivers can count on all the support of the Portuguese government in the resolution of this problem," he told reporters in the northern city of Oporto.
A strike by French truckers last November paralysed 90 percent of the Portuguese truck fleet.
